## E2/E3 — Cost curve and OOM recovery

**The Stream-CQSA rows are all streamed** (host-resident Q/K/V) — that is what the method is. The all-on-GPU variant is excluded from every table: it needs the whole input set resident *and* adds an accumulator, so it OOMs before the baselines it exists to rescue. It remains in the raw JSONL.

The axis that does vary is **where the fp32 accumulator lives**:

| | accumulator | behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `acc=GPU` | device | faster, but the accumulator is an O(N) *device* term that no depth of decomposition shrinks — so it OOMs first, and it OOMs **in the accumulation phase** rather than in the attention kernel |
| `acc=CPU` | host | slower per subproblem, but removes that term entirely and so survives to the largest N — the safe default |

One ladder N ∈ {8K, 16K, 32K, 64K, 128K, 256K, 512K, 1M, 2M, 4M, 8M, 16M}, both precisions, both directions. E2 (overhead where the baseline runs) and E3 (recovery past the wall) are the same sweep — the boundary is a point on the curve, not a separate experiment.

### OOM boundary

| method | fwd: last OK | fwd: OOM at | bwd: last OK | bwd: OOM at |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SDPA | 8M | 16M | 4M | 8M |
| SDPA (mem-eff.) | 8M | 16M | 4M | 8M |
| FlashAttention-2 | 8M | 16M | 4M | 8M |
| Stream-CQSA acc=GPU itr=1 | 8M | 16M | 8M | 16M |
| Stream-CQSA acc=GPU itr=2 | 8M | — | 8M | — |

*(fp16; bf16 boundaries are identical — memory does not depend on which 16-bit type is used.)*

## Gaps and caveats

**10 cells not yet measured** at N ≥ 8M. The main sweep ran before OOM-retirement was made `itr`-aware, so an `itr=1` OOM suppressed `itr=2` at the same N, and it predated the `cqsa_hostmin` (host accumulator) configuration. Job `cqsa_gapfill` refills them; rerun this generator afterwards.

| dtype | dir | N | method family |
|---|---|---|---|
| bf16 | bwd | 16M | Stream-CQSA acc=GPU |
| bf16 | bwd | 16M | FlashAttention-2 |
| bf16 | bwd | 16M | SDPA |
| bf16 | bwd | 16M | SDPA (mem-eff.) |
| bf16 | fwd | 16M | Stream-CQSA acc=GPU |
| fp16 | bwd | 16M | Stream-CQSA acc=GPU |
| fp16 | bwd | 16M | FlashAttention-2 |
| fp16 | bwd | 16M | SDPA |
| fp16 | bwd | 16M | SDPA (mem-eff.) |
| fp16 | fwd | 16M | Stream-CQSA acc=GPU |

**Memory metrics.** `peak` is `torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated()` (live tensors: reproducible, excludes allocator cache and CUDA context). The raw rows also carry `mem_reserved_peak` (what the allocator held from the driver — closer to real device pressure, and typically far larger), plus `mem_inputs_dev` / `mem_workspace` / `mem_host_bytes`. Quote `peak` when comparing methods and `reserved` when discussing how close a run sits to the card's limit; they answer different questions.

**Stage totals** (`stage_ms`) come from CUDA events. With several subproblems in flight an event span also covers time queued behind other streams, so the stages over-count wall clock and are a breakdown of where work is issued, not an additive partition of the measured runtime.

**Warm-up.** The main sweep used `--warmup 0`, correct where one call takes minutes but contaminating at small N, where the first call of each method carries CUDA context and kernel load (FlashAttention read 12,090 ms at N=8192 against a true 0.73 ms). The `rewarm` run re-measured N ≤ 256K with `--warmup 2 --reps 3` and supersedes those rows (later run wins on a duplicate key).

**Figures** are generated from the same data by `benchmarks/make_figures.py` into `docs/figures/`.
